definition_title: Monomials and regularity on projective coordinate charts
natural_language_statement: A degree-d monomial on a finite index type is an integer exponent function whose exponents sum to d. A Laurent expression is a finitely supported coefficient function on such monomials, and RegularOn s requires every monomial with nonzero coefficient to have negative exponents only at indices in s. If the index type is nonempty and d is nonnegative, every degree-d monomial has at least one nonnegative coordinate.
explanation: The definitions encode homogeneous monomials and the support condition used on coordinate charts in the projective-monomial Cech construction. The existence lemma follows because a nonempty finite sum of strictly negative integer exponents would be negative, contradicting the nonnegative total degree.
